rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-eight builder trees go (a row of corals, torrey pines and queen palms every 6 m along the back fences, palms 3-3.4 m from the house fronts, jacarandas, a magnolia and corals by the seating); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the adirondack chair, a beach umbrella, on the open lot corner, and in two back yards.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 12 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the open lot corner, 20 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the north back yard with the adirondack chair: a jacaranda to sit under
the next back yard, 8 m from the house: the yard's tree
the west yard by the closed beach umbrella: a magnolia over the lounging spot
the west end of the north back fence row, 5.3 m from the house: the row's one tree
